description.en: Matching is half the job — the other half is rewriting. re.sub finds every match and replaces it, powering redaction, formatting, and cleanup. Build a digit-masker and wield it.

story_variants.en:
## Search-and-Replace, Supercharged

"`str.replace` swaps one fixed string," Vaathiyaar says. "**`re.sub`** swaps everything matching a *pattern* — so you can redact every phone number, collapse whitespace, or reformat dates in one call. It's the workhorse of text cleanup."

### The Shape of re.sub

```
re.sub(pattern, replacement, text)
```

It scans `text`, and every place `pattern` matches, it substitutes `replacement`. Want to mask every run of digits with `#`? The pattern `\d+` matches one-or-more digits; replace with `'#'`:

```
re.sub(r'\d+', '#', 'Call 5551234')  ->  'Call #'
```

`\d` is "any digit", `+` is "one or more", so `\d+` grabs a whole number as one match — replaced by a single `#`. This is exactly how log scrubbers redact PII and how formatters normalize messy input.

> **Vaathiyaar's note:** always use a raw string `r'...'` for patterns so backslashes mean regex, not Python escapes. `r'\d+'` is the digit pattern; `'\d+'` would confuse the two.

Today you implement `mask_digits(text)` — replace every run of digits with a single `#`.

explanation.en: Replace every run of digits with a single #

instruction.en: Implement `mask_digits(text)` using `re.sub`: replace every run of one-or-more digits (`\d+`) with a single `#`. Then print `mask_digits('Call 555-1234 now')` (expected: `Call #-# now`).

uth_example:
import re

note = "Call Ravi at 98400-12345 on 2025-03-14, mail ravi@example.com"

redacted = re.sub(r"\d{5}-\d{5}", "[phone]", note)
redacted = re.sub(r"[\w.]+@[\w.]+", "[email]", redacted)
indian_date = re.sub(r"(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})", r"\3/\2/\1", redacted)   # backreferences

def shout(match):                        # a function can build each replacement
    return match.group(0).upper()

final = re.sub(r"\bravi\b", shout, indian_date, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
print(redacted)
print(final)

under_the_hood.summary: re.sub finds each non-overlapping match from left to right and replaces it with either a template, whose \1 and \g<name> references are filled from the match's groups, or the return value of a function called with the Match object.

steps.title: Scan, replace, copy the gaps
steps.body: `re.sub(r'\d+', '#', 'Call 5551234 or 911')` finds '5551234', copies 'Call ', adds '#', continues after the match, finds '911', copies ' or ', adds '#', and finally copies whatever text remains. The original string is not modified; a new string is returned.

steps.title: The template is parsed once
steps.body: A replacement string such as `r'\2/\g<y>'` is parsed into literal pieces and group references before the scan starts. For each match the references are filled in: with `(?P<y>\d{4})-(\d\d)` on '2026-06' the result is '06/2026'. `\g<0>` inserts the whole match.

right.label: Filled with
right.code:
text of group 1, group 2
text of a named group
the whole match
a newline character

steps.title: A function replacement
steps.body: If the replacement is callable, re.sub calls it once per match with the Match object and uses whatever string it returns. That lets you compute replacements: `re.sub(r'\d+', lambda m: str(int(m.group()) * 2), 'a1 b22')` gives 'a2 b44'.

props.code:
def mask(m):
    digits = m.group()
    return '*' * (len(digits) - 4) + digits[-4:]

re.sub(r'\d{8,}', mask, 'card 4111111111111111')

stepDescriptions.description: re.sub finds each long digit run.
mask receives the Match and reads its text.

steps.title: count, subn and empty matches
steps.body: `count=1` stops after the first replacement; `re.subn` returns the new string and how many replacements happened. A pattern that can match empty text matches between characters too: `re.sub('x*', '-', 'abc')` gives '-a-b-c-'.

steps.title: Raw strings protect backslashes
steps.body: Write both the pattern and the template as raw strings. In a normal string, '\1' is the character with code 1, not a group reference, and '\d' only works by accident.

under_the_hood.takeaway: re.sub is a left-to-right scan that rebuilds the string from gaps and replacements. Use templates for rearranging groups and a function when the replacement needs logic.
